newsitem.title: USA: IMF chief sees Italy meeting Maastricht target.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief sees Italy meeting Maastricht target.

text.p: IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday it should be possible for Italy to meet a Maastricht treaty condition on budget deficits by 1997.

"Italy is making important efforts to stabilise its economy and to put in place for 1997 a budget which, provided it is fully implemented, makes it possible for Italy to converge and meet the Maastricht criteria on budget deficits," Camdessus told a news conference at the end of the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

Countries wanting to join monetary union from its 1999 start have to cut their budget deficits to no more than three percent of gross domestic product by 1997, as well as reach a number of other economic targets.
But Camdessus urged Italy to reveal details of its proposed budget plan relating to taxes.
"This part of the package is not yet fully disclosed," he said. "Our recommendation to the Italian authorities is to define it as soon as possible."
Camdessus said that those missing details were why he has a "little bit of reservation" about Italy's budget plans.
He added that the spat this week between France and Italy over Rome's chances of meeting the Maastricht treaty will not threaten the viability of Europe's plan for a single currency.

The dispute arose after French President Jacques Chirac on Tuesday publicly questioned Italy's fitness to join Europe's new currency from its planned start in January 1999. Chirac later reversed himself following stiff protests from Italy.
